KMRP optional Xbox Controls integration
========================================

Controller module
-----------------
Name: KPM - Xbox Controls for KOTOR 1 1.2
Author: Saul0097 / scopeking0117-alt
Source: https://github.com/scopeking0117-alt/KPM-Xbox-Controls-K1
Source commit: 78e7eaa3b9554ec0e6732f749424dc916f3a1895

Licence and provenance
----------------------
The controller module is a derivative of ExpandedKeyboardControl, a patch that
lives inside the KOTOR Patch Manager repository and is therefore covered by that
project's MIT licence. Saul0097 stated the derivation directly: "I built the
controller mod starting with j's enhanced keyboard, so that's why I have to make
sure to ask." The two source trees carry the same file set --
<name>.cpp, exports.def, kotor1.hooks.toml, kotor2-gog-aspyr.hooks.toml and
manifest.toml -- which matches that account.

  ExpandedKeyboardControl  https://github.com/LaneDibello/Kotor-Patch-Manager
                           /tree/master/Patches/ExpandedKeyboardControl
                           contributed by "J", merged as #136
  Licence                  MIT, "Copyright (c) 2025 Lane Dibello and KotOR Patch
                           Manager contributors" -- the contributors clause
                           covers J's patch. Full text in
                           LICENSE-KOTOR-PATCH-MANAGER.txt.

Every party in that chain gave permission for KMRP to bundle the result, in the
KOTOR modding Discord #mod_development on 2026-09-04:

  Lane Dibello  "If they want to use or mess with the patches that's fine. It's
                all spelled out in our License."
  J             "yeah i don't mind. It's open source and under the license
                posted above."
  Saul0097      "alright then you're good to go."

Saul0097's own repository still carries no standalone LICENSE file. That does
not leave the integration unlicensed -- the inherited work is MIT and his
permission is explicit and recorded above -- but a LICENSE file in his
repository would state the terms for his own additions in his own words rather
than by inference, and has been requested.

Runtime hook engine
-------------------
Name: KOTOR Patch Manager
Author: Lane Dibello and contributors
Source: https://github.com/LaneDibello/Kotor-Patch-Manager
Source commit: 7d53e52f55622a48ab97001c2680fd9fb59c8f98
License: MIT; full text in LICENSE-KOTOR-PATCH-MANAGER.txt

kmrp-controller-runtime.asi was compiled as 32-bit C++17 with the MSVC static
runtime from the KotorPatcher sources at the commit above. It imports only
KERNEL32.dll. SHA-256:
F5CF2A21E4C28DA95CD8DAAF2704F871A6105616BFE250361929C61BCDB43B45

KMRP applies the source-level change recorded in KMRP-RUNTIME-PATCH.diff so the
runtime discovers its own directory from the address of SelfModuleDir instead
of assuming the DLL is named KotorPatcher.dll. This permits the runtime to be
loaded under the collision-resistant name kmrp-controller-runtime.asi.

kmrp-controller.module is built by src/controller-native/build.cmd as 32-bit
C++17 with the MSVC static runtime, from KMRP's own sources (K1NativeJoystick,
K1ControllerBackend, K1ControllerLayout, K1Rumble) and Saul0097's files at the commit above
as modified by KMRP (src/controller-native/vendor/, exports.def,
kotor1.hooks.toml). The module in the installer built on 2026-09-24 (SHA-256
ECA3DE4BB4845D514B1234F3A546A11790A4297CF4D2D89363F40B73C1C5FE00) is 181,248
bytes and imports XINPUT1_4.dll, GDI32.dll, USER32.dll and KERNEL32.dll. SHA-256:
AC2C41EC4C935B19EFF4693E3FBB43D176D28C5B37DE0CDC2C706F72379652C9
The module in the installer built on 2026-09-25 (SHA-256
B599303AE74DEE5CDA5491E22EC9E173B3E4313ECE88CC8D0EC9A05F55C57108) has SHA-256
DC06F697EE284D93425DCF3FFC965104DCBCD4B9AF681EF4FDD48AEB765CE807. With BioWare's
rumble table added the same day, in the installer
873A01E22D993F91417F8E70E714147A74A89408CA80A09CDACF880622136870, it has SHA-256
E0B62065A20ACC8D957B081EA14F57B5CA5FE62DF1BDF21980F919D590B2B680. With the
rumble mixer and Enhanced haptics (K1Rumble) added the same day, in the
hardware-test installer
C796489A2A5C91D69036C285E1172C3EAFD0F369B0367135719F210015F5FDFC, it is 204,288 bytes
with SHA-256 E52826A2724038E765DFD45B86171160A017E054E346E29CF4A1CE5D0F74DE21.
In the installer D407BF3AC0D7C74247105365AA27660FC18853F977B06EFC629EB6801633F08D, built the same
day with the settings screens' controller glyphs and the status summary's
layout, it is 216,576 bytes with SHA-256

In the installer 128CDC798E061F19CEAEFEF6B6587CAD49C91A1746A419AD079A32A23CE7404D,
built on 2026-09-26 with the Level Up, Auto Level Up and skill-info notice

In the installer D6E40FAFCE9BF7BB0B8B190102BEF984FE454F5683BC3B96C0B14330A0EC628F,
built the same day with the KPM edition beside it, and inside that edition's

0C89C330245F752A303A22D5B731C2E16D19D4731078413B195F01C71972E955.

KMRP's changes to Saul0097's five files are recorded in
KMRP-CONTROLLER-MODULE.diff, generated against the upstream commit above.
Applied to a checkout of that commit it reproduces all five tracked files
exactly (checked 2026-09-24; again on 2026-09-25 after the haptics hooks,
when four files matched byte for byte and exports.def matched in content, the
check's checkout having written it with CRLF endings where the tracked copy
has LF; again after the character-creation guard hooks, and again on
2026-09-26 after the Level Up and notice badges, and twice on 2026-09-28,
after the echo guard and the arrows' removal, after the runtime's `install`
key, and after its `kpm_provided_by` key, with the same result);
regenerate it whenever they change. What the
module does -- the native joystick path, the XInput/SDL backend, the button
prompts and the Controller Layout screen -- is documented in
docs/controller-support.md. It writes no controller-specific bytes to
swkotor.exe: every hook is an entry in patch_config.toml, applied at run time.

History. The kmrp-controller.module in this folder (131,072 bytes, SHA-256
47B9436499CECE7F5BF2E92B936F46B8C036F6BFAE9806973B3F47B9F0257383, importing
USER32.dll and KERNEL32.dll) is the first integration build, of 2026-09-06, and
KMRP-CONTROLLER-PROMPTS-PATCH.diff the changes it carried: connection state,
telling the module's own keystrokes from the keyboard's, button fills on ten
controls, a movie-frame detour and repeating D-pad taps. Neither is used by the
build; both are kept as the record of that first version.

Corrected 2026-09-24: until then this file described that first build as the
module KMRP ships, and KMRP-RUNTIME-PATCH.diff did not hold the runtime change
the paragraph above describes. Commit 2f2206c (2026-09-07) had overwritten that
16-line SelfModuleDir patch with the controller delta, which then went stale as
the module grew. The runtime patch is restored from commit 066b7b1, and the
controller delta has a file of its own.

The `.module` extension is deliberate. It is a PE DLL loaded by the KPM runtime,
but must not also be discovered independently by the ASI loader.
